title: SYSK Selects: Prisons - Not as Fun as You'd Think
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode "Prisons: Not as Fun as You'd Think" (originally aired August 2010). Chuck introduces it as a favorite and an honest look at US prisons. The hosts cover prison statistics and incarceration rates, security levels (minimum, medium, maximum, and supermax/the "Whole"), the history and harms of solitary confinement, the transport and intake process ("fish tank"), prison jobs and pay, daily life, the commissary, black-market goods and pruno, visitation and conjugal visits, prison rape and the Prison Rape Elimination Act, guard abuse and discipline, the Attica and New Mexico prison uprisings, reentry, education, recidivism, costs, and prison movies. The episode ends with a movie list and a listener-mail note.
rerun_of: Prisons: Not as Fun as You'd Think

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces this SYSK Selects episode on prisons. The hosts open with banter about crack-cocaine sentencing disparities, mass incarceration numbers, and Georgia having the highest share of adults in prison.

segments.title: Security levels and supermax prisons
segments.summary: The hosts describe minimum, medium, and maximum security prisons. They explain how the 1999 Marion, Illinois lockdown led to supermax prisons, and how solitary confinement (the 'whole', or SHU) became controversial, with suicides and self-harm cited.

segments.title: Getting to prison and the fish tank
segments.summary: The hosts describe transport to prison, including the 'Diesel to Diesel' prison bus, and intake processing. New inmates ('fish') are segregated for about thirty days in the 'fish tank', where they are watched by others.

segments.title: Prison jobs, cells, and daily counts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss prison jobs paying very little, such as a dorm janitor job paying forty cents a day. They describe cell size, overcrowding, cell blocks, guard control rooms, and head counts.

segments.title: Commissary, black market, and pruno
segments.summary: The hosts describe the prison commissary and its debit ID-card accounts, the black market for cigarettes and favors, and pruno, a homemade prison wine.

segments.title: Visitation and conjugal visits
segments.summary: The hosts explain visitation rules, approved visitor lists, searches, and the extended family program in which married prisoners can have conjugal visits. They note this is available in only a few states, and mention rules on visitor dress and the California domestic partner context.

segments.title: Sexual abuse, guard misconduct, and discipline
segments.summary: The hosts discuss prison rape statistics, including differing survey numbers, the Prison Rape Elimination Act, guard misconduct, and disciplinary 'shots' that affect parole. They also describe unofficial guard punishments.

segments.title: Prison uprisings: Attica and New Mexico
segments.summary: The hosts discuss prison riots, including the 1971 Attica uprising in New York, where guards and prisoners died when the state stormed the prison, and the 1980 New Mexico State Penitentiary riot, where inmates were killed and tortured.

segments.title: Reentry, education, recidivism, and costs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss prisoner reentry, GED and vocational education programs, prison reform, recidivism rates, and the cost of incarceration compared with probation.

segments.title: Prison movies
segments.summary: The hosts list favorite prison films, including Shawshank Redemption, Escape from Alcatraz, Papillon, Cool Hand Luke, Bad Boys, American History X, Animal Factory, and Midnight Express.

segments.title: Listener mail note and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts say there is no listener mail this week and invite listeners to send mail to the show address. The episode closes.
